about-hitomi.body.01: Have you ever wished the records you keep in separate places could be brought together? This care software is designed for care providers, aiming to bring care records, accounting, human resources and more into one place. With connected records, it helps take a little of the workload off the floor.
about-hitomi.body.02: Care settings continue to face staff shortages. Is paperwork such as records and forms also taking up your time? More and more providers now use care software, but much of the data entry is still done by hand, and the repeated effort of copying the same content again and again tends to remain a burden.
about-hitomi.body.03: Source: Ministry of Health, Labour and Welfare, "FY2021 ICT Adoption Support Programme: Summary of Reported Effects" (recording time, information sharing, and improved quality of support)
about-hitomi.body.04: Have you thought about the fact that the working-age generation supporting care is shrinking? The working-age population is projected to fall by around 17%, from about 71.70 million in 2025 to about 59.78 million in 2040. At the same time the number of older people is rising, with the population aged 65 and over expected to peak at about 39.53 million in 2043. To keep providing support with limited staff, isn't making work more efficient through better systems more important than ever?
about-hitomi.body.05: Current figures: Ministry of Internal Affairs and Communications, "Population Estimates" as of 1 October 2024 / Peak: National Institute of Population and Social Security Research, "Population Projections for Japan (2023 projection)"
about-hitomi.body.06: Sources: Cabinet Office, "Annual Report on the Ageing Society 2025" and other future projections; the ageing rate is from the National Institute of Population and Social Security Research, "Population Projections for Japan (2023 projection)" (figures change depending on the assumptions used)
about-hitomi.body.07: What if care records, accounting, human resources, shift planning and the rest were all in one place? This care software aims to bring together software that used to be separate. By reusing what you have entered once, you may be able to cut out re-entering the same names and figures over and over. And because the records gather in one place, handovers and checks become easier too.
about-hitomi.body.08: Daily records and handovers in one place. It becomes easier to look things up later and to hand over to colleagues.
about-hitomi.body.09: Billing and payment management in one place. Information entered once is reused, cutting down on copying.
about-hitomi.body.10: Shift, attendance and payroll information in one place. Monthly preparation and totalling become easier.
about-hitomi.body.11: Shift planning made simple, taking staff preferences and working conditions into account. Less time spent on corrections and adjustments.
about-hitomi.body.12: Communication between staff in one place. Handovers and urgent messages reach everyone quickly.
about-hitomi.body.13: What suits one facility may not suit another. Start with a free consultation, where we can look at your current difficulties together and see whether it is likely to fit. There is no sales pitch.
about-hitomi.body.14: A dedicated member of staff supports you with getting set up and with any questions about how to use it. You can go ahead knowing there is someone to ask when you get stuck.
about-hitomi.body.15: National or local government subsidies may be available. We can also discuss whether you are eligible (requirements change from year to year, so we check the latest information).
about-hitomi.body.16: You do not have to sign up straight away; you can start simply by hearing about it and seeing the screens. It is fine to get in touch while you are still undecided.
about-hitomi.body.17: The email address you enter is used to send you your diagnosis results and to contact you about consultations. We do not use it for other purposes without your consent. Please rest assured that we will not pester you with sales calls.
about-hitomi.body.18: We will not push a sale on you. The diagnosis is first of all a way to learn your own facility's strengths and room to grow, and it is entirely up to you whether to take things further. If anything concerns you, you can ask about it during the consultation.
about-hitomi.body.19: The preparation needed and the way forward differ from facility to facility. You can find out how much effort and time it is likely to take in a free consultation, where we ask about your current situation. We work through it with you, so it is never simply left in your hands.
about-hitomi.body.20: How your existing paper and spreadsheet records can be used depends on your facility's situation. You can go through this together, including how the transfer would work, in a free consultation. There is no need to switch everything over at once.
about-hitomi.body.21: It is designed to be easy to use when you are out and about or making records, but whether it runs smoothly on your equipment depends on your setup. You can check whether it is likely to work on your devices in a free consultation.
about-hitomi.body.22: It also readily supports needs such as viewing several sites together. Exactly what is possible depends on how your organisation is structured, so please check in a free consultation.
about-hitomi.body.23: Whether care software is needed differs from facility to facility.

analysis.body.beaver.0: The "Beaver type, full of skilled hands" is a powerhouse with plenty of qualified professionals and specialists. Certified Care Workers, rehabilitation staff, registered dietitians and more are all in place, so even difficult cases can be handled with reliable skill. That high level of expertise connects directly to claiming care-fee add-ons and to families' trust.
analysis.body.beaver.1: Put that expertise to work in your outreach and recruiting brand, and you become even stronger. Manage the status of qualifications and training with data, and make "you can count on this place" visible to everyone.
analysis.body.fukurou.0: The "Owl type, ahead of the curve" is a wise operator that runs smartly with digital tools. Records and information sharing are systemized, and monitoring sensors and care robots are used with ease. Wasteful work and overtime are few, so you can keep quality high even with limited staff — that is its greatest weapon. Because data naturally accumulates, the cycle of improvement is fast too.
analysis.body.fukurou.1: The key is where to spend the "spare capacity" that efficiency creates. Direct that freed-up time toward attracting residents, developing staff and raising care quality, and the Owl type takes off. Use the data you have built up to make care visible, and you gain clear differentiation from other facilities.
analysis.body.hachi.0: The "Honeybee type, connected to the community" is a type rich in local ties. Welcoming volunteers and trainees, working with the community general support center, disaster-response agreements and joining local events — the facility is open to its town. Being rooted in the community earns trust not only from residents and families but from the whole town.
analysis.body.hachi.1: The key is to make those community ties visible and share them. Record and share the results of your partnerships and activities, and trust spreads even further, leading to referrals, tours and job applications. The community is a facility's greatest ally.
analysis.body.inu.0: A "Dog type, caring for teammates" facility puts the people who work there first. They call out to one another, help each other, and new staff naturally settle in. That kind of atmosphere has surely taken root. Because people stay for the long term, care know-how builds up little by little. A place where staff can work with peace of mind is also a comfortable place for residents. Families' trust, too, is born from these small daily efforts.
analysis.body.inu.1: At the same time, the more a facility runs on people's hard work, the more the burden of records and paperwork tends to land on the floor. Are handwriting, transcription and double entry eating up precious time? Keep this warm teamwork just as it is, and if you can make daily records and procedures a little lighter, staff can face the people in front of them even more. Bringing records together digitally to cut the workload is well within reach even for your floor today. Precisely because people are the lead role here, a system that lets their strength shine more may be the next step.
analysis.body.iruka.0: The "Koala type, the popular one" is a master of attracting residents, chosen again and again by the community. Inquiries never stop coming through referrals and word of mouth, and trust runs so high that there is even a waiting list. The reputation of "that place is reassuring" is an asset above all else. A virtuous cycle where residents bring more residents is this type's strength.
analysis.body.iruka.1: The challenge is how to carry that high popularity into the future. Always being full also means there is demand you cannot fully meet. Step into expansion or new services, and you can turn popularity into growth. Put into words, with data, why you are chosen, and you gain a repeatable system for attracting residents.
analysis.body.kitsune.0: The "Fox type, good with the books" is a management pro, strong on numbers and cash flow. It never misses usable subsidies or programs and steadily builds up profit. It spreads risk across several businesses and makes sound investment decisions. It may not be flashy, but it is firmly laying the foundation for a facility that lasts.
analysis.body.kitsune.1: The challenge is to return that management sense to the floor as well. Even if you are strong on numbers, if staff retention and digital transformation are put off, the floor's fatigue will eventually rebound onto management. Channel the profits you generate into staff pay and digitalization, and strong management and a good floor start to support each other, becoming even more stable.
analysis.body.kuma.0: The "Bear type, safe and secure" is a solid defender that prevents accidents and lets residents spend their days with peace of mind. Systems for accident prevention and emergency response are thorough, with no history of sanctions. It is fully prepared for the unexpected, with liability insurance and more.
analysis.body.kuma.1: Communicating your safety efforts clearly to families raises their trust even further. Share near-miss and accident records digitally, and the precision of prevention improves too.
analysis.body.ookami.0: The "Wolf type, always prepared" is strong on readiness for infectious diseases and disasters. Infection and food-poisoning control, business continuity plans (BCP), stockpiles and drills are all handled without a gap, so it is dependable when it matters. Its everyday carefulness is the power that protects the facility.
analysis.body.ookami.1: Your readiness efforts also work as material for communicating safety and reassurance. Keep your BCP and drill records in order, and your emergency response becomes even faster and more reliable.
analysis.body.penguin.0: The "Penguin type, growing together" is a type with people-development built into its roots. Training, OJT and study sessions are active, newcomers become capable quickly, and specialized learning such as dementia care builds up. A facility where people grow keeps care quality stable and offers reassurance for the future.
analysis.body.penguin.1: The key is to pair developing people with retention — keeping them working there for the long term. When development and retention mesh, a virtuous cycle emerges in which veterans raise the next generation, lifting the whole facility's strength.
analysis.body.risu.0: The "Squirrel type, proud of its meals" is a type that values nutritional care and the joy of eating. Systems for nutrition reviews and oral care tailored to each person are in place, supporting health and satisfaction through "eating." A strong reputation for meals is a major strength that can decide which facility people choose.
analysis.body.risu.1: Combine your strength in food with seasonal event meals and little pleasures, and its appeal grows further. Digitalize your nutrition and oral-care records, and you can balance care-fee add-ons with quality while extending your strength even more.
analysis.body.usagi.0: The "Rabbit type, full of momentum" is a fast-growing type where both locations and revenue keep climbing. It takes on new services and initiatives one after another and does not fear change. With the speed to turn local needs into reality quickly, it is the facility whose future is the most exciting. The momentum itself is an appeal that draws in staff and residents alike.
analysis.body.usagi.1: Behind rapid growth, the thing to watch is whether the floor's "systems" keep pace with expansion. If staff retention and the standardization of records and training are put off, the bill comes due as uneven quality or turnover. Now, while you are growing, is the chance to put the foundations in order. Once the base is solid, growth accelerates even more.
analysis.body.zou.0: The "Elephant type, easy to work at" is skilled at building a workplace that is kind to staff. Overtime is low, and days off and paid leave are easy to take. Programs such as childcare leave are in place, and flexible working styles support diverse ways of working. Being easy to work at is a major weapon for staff retention and recruiting.
analysis.body.zou.1: Share that ease of working on your recruiting page and more, and applications gather more easily. Manage shifts and leave digitally, and you can keep the workplace easy to work at even during busy periods.
analysis.combo.fukurou_kitsune: Computers and smartphones are used for records and sharing information, which cuts out wasted effort, and that in turn leaves room to look properly at the numbers. Lighter paperwork may well be part of what makes the operation feel so settled.
analysis.combo.hachi_inu: The facility is trusted by the community and by families, and staff stay for a long time. From outside come referrals from people who say "that place is reliable", and inside, familiar faces support the residents. This may be a facility where peace of mind is in place both outside and in.
analysis.combo.inu_zou: Because it is easy to take time off and possible to work without strain, staff are less likely to leave, and because the faces stay the same, new people also find it easier to keep going. Sudden absences, for example, can be covered by helping each other out, and that sense of security leads back to staff staying. These two strengths may be working well together.
analysis.combo.kitsune_iruka: Beds and service slots being well filled forms the base of the monthly income, and that stability makes it possible to decide calmly about replacing equipment or adding staff. Finances and occupancy may well be turning together like two wheels.
analysis.combo.kuma_ookami: The facility is good both at preventing everyday falls and near-misses and at preparing for emergencies such as earthquakes or sudden illness. From small day-to-day observations through to emergency procedures, this may be a facility that thinks everything through in terms of "safety".
analysis.combo.penguin_beaver: Because the facility has both the ability to develop people and specialists such as nurses and rehabilitation staff, new people can grow while asking about anything they do not understand on the spot. The quality of care may well be becoming more solid, step by step.
analysis.combo.penguin_zou: First there is a foundation where staff can work without strain, and on top of that there is room to take time teaching new people properly. In a field where training easily gets pushed aside by busyness, these strengths may have come together in just the right order.

analysis.high.beaver: Perhaps this is because specialists in nursing, rehabilitation, consultation and other areas are all in place, so it is clear who to ask about what. If someone is unsure about a wound or a medication, for example, they can turn to a nurse; if a resident's movement is declining, they can turn to the rehabilitation staff, and ask right there and then. Difficult cases may not have to be carried alone.
analysis.high.fukurou: Perhaps this is because handovers and near-miss reports reach everyone straight away by phone or computer, so fewer things get missed and nobody has to wonder "did I mention that?". Even a handover after a night shift, for example, can be checked later on a phone by anyone who could not be there. Time spent hunting for records in piles of paper may also be short.
analysis.high.hachi: Perhaps this is because the facility has built relationships where nearby families, hospitals and care managers say "that place is reliable". Enquiries about people being discharged, for example, may come directly from hospitals, and requests for tours keep coming by word of mouth. Events and community gatherings may also be welcomed as a matter of course.
analysis.high.inu: Perhaps this is because many staff have worked there a long time, so residents can relax and rely on "the usual people". A resident greeting someone by name first thing in the morning, for example, is possible because the faces do not change. Even when new people join, there may be an atmosphere that helps them stay.
analysis.high.iruka: Perhaps beds and service slots are well filled, so that "as soon as a place opens up, the next person is decided". Even when one person leaves, for example, the next is settled quickly through someone who was waiting or a referral from a care manager. There may be a real sense of being needed and chosen by the local community.
analysis.high.kitsune: Perhaps this is because the financial outlook is clear, so the facility can run without worrying every month about whether it will get through the next one. Because the monthly income and expenditure are understood, for example, decisions about replacing equipment or adding staff can be made without panic. There may also be room to direct money where it is needed.
analysis.high.kuma: Perhaps this is because near-misses are shared immediately and discussed all the way through to "how do we prevent it next time?". If there are two near-misses in the same corridor, for example, the discussion moves the same day to reviewing the handrails or the flooring. All the staff may know which places and times of day carry the most risk of falls.
analysis.high.ookami: Perhaps this is because it is decided who does what in an earthquake, a sudden fever or an infection outbreak, so people can act calmly when it matters. Even if a resident develops a fever in the night, for example, it is settled who contacts the family and who arranges the medical visit. Evacuation routes and the order of contacts may be checked together by everyone.
analysis.high.penguin: Perhaps this is because senior staff stay close to new arrivals and teach the steps of the work one by one, rather than leaving them to "watch and learn". On someone's first day helping with bathing, for example, a senior colleague goes in alongside them, talking them through it, then reviews afterwards with advice on what to do differently. There may be an atmosphere where nobody is left alone after just a few days.
analysis.high.risu: Perhaps this is because staff notice how much each person eats and how well they swallow, so they quickly spot when someone has not been eating much lately. If a resident eats little for several days, for example, staff can respond in a way that suits that person, changing how food is chopped or thickened, or adding a favourite dish. It may also be clear who to consult about nutrition.
analysis.high.usagi: Perhaps this is because the facility is open to new methods and new services, with an atmosphere where people can say "let's just try it". When a local need is noticed, for example, something is started small and then widened while watching how it goes. A good reputation may be spreading, and the facility may be steadily adding to what it can do.
analysis.high.zou: Perhaps this is because shift requests are usually granted, days off can really be taken, and staff can work without strain. Even a day off needed for a child's school event or a hospital visit, for example, can be arranged if mentioned early. Staff may genuinely feel that this is an easy place to work.
analysis.low.beaver: Is it all the facility can manage to get through daily care with few hands, leaving no time to think about how qualified staff are assigned and what roles they play? When someone is unsure about a wound or a medication, there is nobody inside the facility to ask right away. Is that uneasy feeling familiar?
analysis.low.fukurou: Are daily logs and shifts still handled on paper, so that pulling everything together at the end of the month takes a long time? What happened during the day is left on paper for the night staff, and then typed into a computer all over again. Does the effort of writing the same thing twice pile up day after day?
analysis.low.hachi: Is the facility so taken up with the care in front of it that there is no chance to let people outside know about it? Good care is being provided, yet tours and word of mouth are slow to increase, and that quality is not reaching the people around you. Does that feel like a missed opportunity?
analysis.low.inu: Do people join and then leave again and again, so that each time you are chasing recruitment and starting the training over? Someone finally becomes fully capable and then resigns, and you have to advertise and teach from scratch again. Does the burden on those who remain grow every time an experienced colleague leaves?
analysis.low.iruka: Are there still empty beds or service slots, and does it worry you when they are not filled? Income falls with every vacancy, and yet the quality of the care being provided has not reached the people who need it. Does that ring true?
analysis.low.kitsune: Are you so busy with daily work that taking time to look properly at the numbers keeps getting put off? Things carry on with only a rough sense of the finances, and it is only at the year-end accounts that the rise in labour or utility costs becomes clear. Is that a worry?
analysis.low.kuma: Are near-miss reports written up, but never revisited because there is no time? Once filled in they sit in a box, and falls and near-misses keep happening in the same place and at the same time of day, only with a different name attached. Does that sound familiar?
analysis.low.ookami: Is there an emergency manual that stays tucked away, with few people able to say what is in it? Only after someone develops a fever at night does anyone start hurriedly turning the pages of the procedures. Has it stayed a case of "we'll think about it when it happens"?
analysis.low.penguin: When new people join, are the ones who should teach them too busy, so the day ends with "just watch from the side for now"? They are left to copy what they see during their first bathing assistance, and are told afterwards that they did it wrong. Does what is taught differ from person to person, so the answer changes depending on who is asked?
analysis.low.risu: Are meal records kept only roughly as "all" or "half", so that weight loss is noticed too late? By the time anyone realises, the person's trousers have become loose. And is it still unclear who to consult about nutrition?
analysis.low.usagi: Are you so busy with daily work that it is hard to find time to start anything new? An idea comes up that you would like to try, but the daily rush carries it away and nothing happens. Is there that frustration of wanting to change something but not being able to move?
analysis.low.zou: Every time someone calls in sick, does another person come in to cover, making time off harder to take? The phone rings on your day off and you are called in; overtime and taking work home become normal. Do you start the next day still tired?

dyn.axfix.inu.evidence: Of providers whose turnover fell, 63.6% cited "improved workplace relationships" as the reason (Care Work Foundation, FY2023 survey).
dyn.axfix.inu.step: Put one thing in place: training, or a path to keep working long-term
dyn.axfix.inu.why: When staff keep turning over, hard-won know-how and knowledge never take root, and care quality becomes uneven.
dyn.axfix.iruka.benefit: Inquiries increase, and your vacancies fill up
dyn.axfix.iruka.evidence: One analysis finds that profitable day-care facilities secure registered users at more than 2.5 times their capacity (Welfare and Medical Service Agency (WAM), management analysis).
dyn.axfix.iruka.step: Set up your tour flow and your website and social media presence
dyn.axfix.iruka.why: If you have vacancies but the facility is not well known, then even with the strength to be chosen, residents will not gather.
dyn.axfix.kitsune.benefit: Profit grows, creating room to invest
dyn.axfix.kitsune.evidence: Of providers not claiming add-ons, 85.8% cite "cumbersome paperwork such as care plans" as the reason (Ministry of Health, Labour and Welfare, FY2024 survey). Lighten the paperwork and you can stop missing out.
dyn.axfix.kitsune.step: Review the subsidies and add-ons you are missing out on
dyn.axfix.kitsune.why: When you miss out on the programs and subsidies you could use, the profit you should have gained never reaches you.
dyn.axfix.kuma.benefit: Prevent accidents and raise families' peace of mind
dyn.axfix.kuma.step: Put in place systems for sharing near-misses and preventing accidents
dyn.axfix.kuma.why: If accident prevention and emergency readiness are weak, it can lead to serious accidents and a loss of trust.
dyn.axfix.ookami.benefit: Become a reassuring facility that is strong even in a crisis
dyn.axfix.ookami.step: Put in place your BCP, infection control, stockpiles and drills
dyn.axfix.ookami.why: If your readiness for infectious diseases and disasters is insufficient, keeping the operation running becomes difficult when it matters.
dyn.axfix.penguin.benefit: People grow quickly, and care quality stays stable
dyn.axfix.penguin.step: Put your training plans and development records in order
dyn.axfix.penguin.why: When development is ad hoc, it takes newcomers longer to become fully capable, and care quality becomes uneven.
dyn.axfix.risu.benefit: Balance meal satisfaction with care-fee add-ons
dyn.axfix.risu.step: Put your nutrition and oral-care records and systems in order
dyn.axfix.risu.why: When nutrition and oral-care systems are weak, you miss out on residents' health and satisfaction and on chances to claim add-ons.
dyn.axfix.usagi.step: Plan one new service or capacity expansion
dyn.axfix.usagi.why: If your scale and new challenges stay flat, your presence in the community slowly fades.
dyn.axfix.zou.benefit: Overtime falls, and being easy to work at draws people in
dyn.axfix.zou.evidence: Of providers working on retention, 52.5% offer "flexible working hours and days off based on staff wishes" and 44.8% promote "cutting overtime and taking paid leave" (Care Work Foundation, FY2023 survey).
dyn.axfix.zou.step: Digitalize the management of shifts and leave
dyn.axfix.zou.why: When overtime is high and time off is hard to take, the burden on staff piles up, leading to turnover and difficulty recruiting.

guide.body.02: The strengths that scored highly are your facility's pride. Try saying so directly when showing people round or in your job adverts.
guide.body.03: The strengths that scored lower are not grounds for blame; they are the areas you can build on. We suggest choosing just one to work on first.

hiyari.body.01: Small observations, added up, keep accidents at bay. Someone nearly fell. Someone almost handed over the wrong medicine. It did not turn into a serious accident, but it gave you a fright. Each of those moments may be an important clue to preventing the next one.
hiyari.body.02: Most accidents, it is said, do not happen out of nowhere. More often than not, there were several small close calls beforehand.
hiyari.body.03: That is exactly why it matters to record near-misses and look back over them together. In a busy workplace, though, things like this tend to happen.
hiyari.body.04: What matters is that people can note down what they noticed without hesitation, and that everyone can see the same information. When it is clear that this is not about blame but about sharing in order to prevent the next incident, reports come more easily. A near-miss is an early warning from the floor. A system that picks up those voices leads to a facility where everyone feels safe.

intro.body.02: Using the information on care facilities published by the government (the Long-Term Care Service Information Disclosure System), we score 12 strengths automatically. There is no need to answer questions as you would in a survey or a test. You can even see where your facility stands (as a standard score) among facilities in the same area and the same service category.
intro.body.03: Where do your facility's strengths lie? And where is the room to grow? How do you stand compared with facilities in the same area and the same category? Your animal type, the balance of your 12 strengths and the badges you earn make it clear at a glance.
intro.body.04: When you take the diagnosis, your facility's strengths and room to grow are shown. You can also see where you stand compared with nearby facilities and with the whole country. You come to know what you are good at and what is going to waste, in numbers rather than by feel. "We are buried in records and paperwork", "adjusting shifts is hard work", "sharing information does not go well"

kadai.body.01: The strains felt on the floor tend to follow a few set patterns. Here we look at four common worries, and at ways of thinking that could make them easier through better systems.
kadai.body.02: The fewer people you have, the more the weight of each individual task tells. Time spent entering the same thing again and again, or hunting for paperwork, may well be reduced with the right systems. In a free consultation, we can look together at where that effort could be cut.
kadai.body.03: Is the time for the care that really matters being eaten away by record-keeping? When information is gathered in one place, it becomes easier to lighten the work of writing, searching and rewriting. We can talk in a free consultation about where things could be made easier first.
kadai.body.04: Sometimes the work you are already doing is not properly reflected in what you are credited for. When information can be seen in one place, it may be easier to notice gaps and oversights. Please check anything that concerns you in a free consultation.
kadai.body.05: A heavy paperwork burden tends to make a workplace harder to work in. If daily tasks become a little easier, staff find it easier to focus on the work they are really there for. You can talk through what might be changed first in a free consultation.
kadai.body.06: If any of these four sound familiar, that is your way into a review.

kazoku.body.02: For a family, the facility caring for someone dear to them is always on their mind. That is exactly why frequent, accurate sharing of information is the basis of trust.
kazoku.body.03: On the floor, though, scenes like these may well come up.
kazoku.body.04: When these things pile up, explaining takes time and families are kept waiting. If each person's records are gathered in one place, whoever takes the call can check straight away how that day has gone. Being able to explain calmly and carefully leads to trust.

kiroku.body.01: It starts with not writing the same thing twice. You provide care, write the records, and then prepare the paperwork for billing. Before you know it, you have spent more of the day at a desk. Does that sound like a familiar day?
kiroku.body.02: Care work brings a great deal of writing with it: daily records, messages, billing paperwork, payroll-related admin. Each one may be small, but together they become a heavy burden.
kiroku.body.03: What tends to weigh most is writing the same information over and over.
kiroku.body.04: This doubled-up effort not only takes time, but also makes mistakes more likely when copying things across. If records, billing and payroll were connected in one place rather than kept separately, information entered once could be used again, and the number of times you have to write things down might fall. That time can then go to the residents in front of you.
